about: Every wire and stored shape: its id, its owning context, its schema, the one codec file that may write it, and the command that checks it. coax/web/tool.sh wire-check holds the tree to this file. How to add a row: proto/README.md, "Register a wire shape". Plan: docs/protocol/2026-11-11-compliance-plan.md.

shapes.note: Everglade's session text frames, hand-packed (30 Hz). Page and room load the same codec file; since E3b (#13364) that holds e xp, e level, e rc, e wm, e mend, e pburn, e pgone, g, v, w, L, V, X and the K reader too.
Everglade's additive J1 mounted-joust input frame (#13244). Page and room load the same codec file.
Everglade II Wild Companion: M1 SEQ FORM SLOT, m1 SEQ FORM, r SEQ familiar. The room reads and writes it through this file; the page still has its own code (#13244, #13245).
Everglade II Find Familiar: M3 SEQ FORM SLOT SPIRIT, m3 SEQ STATUS. The room reads and writes it through this file; the page still has its own code (#13244, #13245).
Everglade II familiar pocket, recall and release: M4 SEQ ORDER, m4 SEQ ORDER. The room reads and writes it through this file; the page still has its own code (#13244, #13245).
Everglade II familiar step: M5 SEQ, m5 SEQ. The room reads and writes it through this file; the page still has its own code (#13244, #13245).
Everglade II familiar touch Cure Wounds: M6 SEQ SEAT, m6 SEQ. The room reads and writes it through this file; the page still has its own code (#13244, #13245).
Everglade II familiar senses: M7 SEQ, m7 SEQ, m8 MODE. The room reads and writes it through this file; the page still has its own code (#13244, #13245).
Everglade II familiar snapshot m2 TICK COUNT [OWNER FORM X Z HP MAX].... The room reads and writes it through this file; the page still has its own code (#13244, #13245).

Everglade II Healer's Kit before wire 7: U1 SEQ, u1 SEQ LEFT, r SEQ kit. The room still reads U1 and writes u1 with it for a wire 6 page, behind the previous wire's hooks (everglade/server/wire-prev.coax, #13398); since wire 7 the ask and the answer are everglade2-familiar-v2's (#13245); docs/protocol/everglade-healers-kit-v1.md.

Everglade II's familiars and Healer's Kit since wire 7 (#13276, #13245): each request an E kind (9 to 15), each answer an e entry of D told to the asker (e fam, e fam-cast, e kit), the familiar itself a row (WK_FAMILIAR, everglade-session-v7). One codec: the page writes the requests and reads the answers with it, the room reads and writes with it; docs/protocol/everglade-familiar-v2.md.

Everglade II riding in wire 7 (#13268): a mount is a row (WK_MOUNT, everglade-session-v7), each ask an E kind (20 mount, 21 get down, 22 land), the answer an e entry of D told to the asker (e ride SEQ CODE MOUNT). One codec: the page writes the asks and reads the answers and rows with it, the room reads and writes with it; docs/protocol/everglade-riding-v1.md.

The relay room's own frames (#13245): y SEAT N T [G], j SEAT, l SEAT, m SEAT TEXT, the clock ping t MS and its pong t MS T. The room (coax/web/room/room-relay.coax) writes them with this file and every page in a relay room reads them with it: everglade/client/net.coax, apps/openagents-web/everglade-net.coax, lockroom.coax and oneshot.coax; docs/protocol/room-relay-v2.md. The rooms list JSON (rm_rooms) is not in it.
Everglade II's path guard (g2, g3) and monsters (h2, h3). The room writes them and the page reads them through this file (#13246); docs/protocol/everglade-guard-monsters-v2.md.

The previous wire, for one release (#13398): what a wire 7 room writes a seat whose hello said wire 6, and reads from it (the familiar frames m1 to m8 and M1 M3 to M7, and the kit's U1 and u1, in place of the rows, E kinds and e entries of #13276). The change that raises WIRE_VERSION again replaces this row and its files; docs/protocol/everglade-previous-wire.md.
Projectiles over a room: F (page to room), a and d (room to pages), pinned in the combat profile beside the creature frames (#13246); docs/protocol/everglade-projectiles-v1.md.

WebTransport framing: the mark byte and channel, 1,200-byte datagrams, and input datagrams that repeat the unacknowledged with the NET_SAME byte (#13176, #13246); docs/protocol/aethyr-transport-v1.md.
The optional latency observation frame @1.
Orbit League's session frames.

Seat ticket v5 (#13260): signed by the API's private key (BIP-340), checked by rooms with public keys only. The API calls the codec through coax/web/api/ticket-sign-unit.c; rooms through room-ticket.coax tk_check_keys.

Seat ticket HMAC v2, v3 and v4 (#13248): written by metaverse-engine/session/seat-ticket.coax seat_ticket_hmac_write (the API calls it) and checked by coax/web/room/room-ticket.coax tk_check, whose signers for dev rooms and checks (tk_sign and the rest) all call seat_ticket_hmac_write. The v4 envelope (resume_ticket_wrap, metaverse-engine/session/resume-envelope.coax) is pinned here too: the fixture's v4 ticket with its durable capture.

What a room shard and the API say to each other outside the session wire (E7 and E8, #13250): the vitals post and its receipt, the directory post, a drain's signed text, the control ask and the lines of its answer, and the checkpoint's receipt. The room writes and reads them through this file, its local stand-in for the API answers with it, and the API writes both receipts through it (coax/web/api/ticket-sign.coax). The API still reads the two posts in C and builds the control answer in SQL (player.c and rooms.c keep their route lines). The fixture holds posts a room wrote and receipts and control answers a running API gave. docs/protocol/room-reports-v1.md.
Durable character resume profile 2 (ingress with sent and stored without sent; #13244).

The Character aggregate (#13290, AAA P4.1; docs/protocol/everglade-character-v1.md): class, XP, the floor level, known abilities, the ledger's bag and version by item ID, equipment, coin and quests, the record the server owns for each character. character.coax writes and reads it and owns its rules (char_level, char_class_set, char_fits, char_accept).

Content tables v1 (#13294, AAA P4.5; docs/protocol/aethyr-content-v1.md): a game's data as versioned tables of rows in one text document, which a room loads at start and Aethyrforge edits on its edit log. tables.coax reads and writes it and refuses a dangling ID, a place out of reach, a sum that is wrong and any bytes but the document's one form. Everglade's tables (creatures, spawns, abilities, items, loot, quests, dialogue, points) are everglade/content/everglade.content, bound by everglade/model/content.coax.

A room's ledger operation and the store's answer (#13291, AAA P4.2; docs/protocol/everglade-item-op-v1.md): loot, quest stages and rewards, and what a character wears, each one operation with an ID (read, grant, consume, claim) and a claim on the character's record applied with it once; the answer is the ledger's status and the character as the store has it (the record, the kinds of its bag, the inventory version). The room posts it to POST /api/playtest/room-items under room-write purpose items; player.c answers through io_answer. The ledger's rules are metaverse-engine/session/ledger.coax's and the record's are everglade/model/character.coax's.

Domain event (#13319, DDD.8): an item was granted to a character. Published by the item ledger's outbox in the grant's transaction (verse.item_outbox, op grant; LedgerEntry in metaverse-engine/session/ledger.coax); a reader takes rows after the last sequence it took (verse.item_outbox_since). Typed IDs only: the sequence, the character, the item, its content kind, the time.

Domain event (#13319, DDD.8): a character's level rose. Published by the characters' outbox (verse.character_outbox, migration 0176) in the transaction that changes the record (player.c character_outbox: a seat ticket, an accepted checkpoint, a ledger operation's XP claim); events.coax ev_levelled decides. A reader takes rows after the last sequence it took (verse.character_outbox_since).
Diagnostic code 1 (#13429, proto/README.md "Diagnostic codes"): link state, retry no. Nothing in the realm's state or content has this id. Fix the id, or author the thing.
Diagnostic code 2 (#13429, proto/README.md "Diagnostic codes"): link spawned, retry yes. It is in the state, and the world builds it at its next commit. Ask again after a frame.
Diagnostic code 3 (#13429, proto/README.md "Diagnostic codes"): link spawned, retry no. The world had no free slot for it. Remove something or raise the world's capacity.
Diagnostic code 4 (#13429, proto/README.md "Diagnostic codes"): link spawned, retry no. It was in the world and was removed: defeated, opened or deleted. It comes back only by a reset or an edit.
Diagnostic code 5 (#13429, proto/README.md "Diagnostic codes"): link view, retry no. It stands outside what the camera sees. Move or turn the camera.
Diagnostic code 6 (#13429, proto/README.md "Diagnostic codes"): link drawn, retry yes. Its draw rows are older than the state. The next frame writes them.
Diagnostic code 7 (#13429, proto/README.md "Diagnostic codes"): link drawn, retry no. The draw list or its store was full, and it was left out. Draw fewer things or raise the limit.
Diagnostic code 8 (#13429, proto/README.md "Diagnostic codes"): link drawn, retry no. The realm or its host hides it now: a mode that doesn't show it, or a host that draws this kind itself.
Diagnostic code 9 (#13429, proto/README.md "Diagnostic codes"): link asset, retry yes. Its mesh, texture or pack is still arriving.
Diagnostic code 10 (#13429, proto/README.md "Diagnostic codes"): link asset, retry no. Its asset was fetched and refused, or the fetch failed.
Diagnostic code 11 (#13429, proto/README.md "Diagnostic codes"): link asset, retry no. Its kind names no asset.
Diagnostic code 12 (#13429, proto/README.md "Diagnostic codes"): link collider, retry no. It should block or be touched, and has no collider.
Diagnostic code 13 (#13429, proto/README.md "Diagnostic codes"): link collider, retry no. It has a collider that doesn't block now.
Diagnostic code 14 (#13429, proto/README.md "Diagnostic codes"): link system, retry yes. The system that moves it hasn't run since it spawned.
Diagnostic code 15 (#13429, proto/README.md "Diagnostic codes"): link system, retry no. The system that moves it is stopped: a mode, a pause or a budget.
Diagnostic code 16 (#13429, proto/README.md "Diagnostic codes"): link runtime, retry no. A budget was reached and work was dropped. The line names the limit and how much was dropped.
Diagnostic code 17 (#13429, proto/README.md "Diagnostic codes"): link runtime, retry no. A pack was read and refused.

Realm frame messages v1 (#13432, docs/metaverse/realm-origin.md): what the site's page and a realm in its sandboxed frame post to each other (window.postMessage): hello and ask from the site, ready, answer and refused from the realm. A realm that runs someone else's code is served from the realm origin with no origin of its own, and these are the only words between the two. The browser glue (coax/web/realm-frame.js, host.js coaxial.framed) carries the text and judges nothing; a realm's module reads and writes it through the codec (Splice: splice_framed).
Durable character resume profile 3 (adds rest and optional uses; #13244).
Room writes v1 (#13260): each shard signs its writes to the API with its own key, the shard and purpose inside the signed bytes; the API checks through ticket-sign-unit.c (rooms.c room_write_signed).

Content numbers (#13286): the number a wire frame or a save carries for an ability (a cast's SLOT in C and e cast), a spell (an event's SPELL), a creature template (a stat block), an item kind and a spawn (h2 and h3's M), each frozen under a key. The registry is the codec; class-kit.coax (xk_wire), creatures.coax (E2M_SPAWN) and the rules' tables are held to it by their checks. wire-check rule 7 fails on a row of the base's copy that is gone or changed. The P frame's content pin is sealed with the table's hash (everglade-wire.coax WIRE_CONTENT_IDS); docs/protocol/everglade-content-ids-v1.md.

Moderation v1 (#13302): a moderator's record (VERB PID MINUTES REASON), a room's command (X and the record), its report to the API (POST /api/playtest/room-mod-log, room-write purpose moderation) and receipt, and the room's answer to the moderator (q). The rules live in the codec file too. The API calls it through coax/web/api/moderation-policy.coax (player.c, room.c).

Crash report v1 (#13298, docs/deployment/crash-reports.md): what a room shard posts to POST /api/playtest/room-crash after a crash (signed as its room-write `crash` purpose), and what the API builds from a page's crash event. room-crash.coax builds a room's report from its handler's dump (room-crash.c) and addr2line's names, builds a page's, and checks and reads both; the API calls it through ticket-sign-unit.c and stores the body whole, by the md5 of its source and sig line.

Crash report v2 (#13379, docs/deployment/crash-reports.md): a page's report whose frames carry their code offsets, `f NAME +0xOFFSET`, so a frame resolves to a Coax line after the fact. The API builds it from a page's crash event (host.js sends each frame as NAME and its offset) and reads v1 and v2; the signature and the bucket are v1's. A room's report stays v1.

Crash report v3 (#13379, docs/deployment/crash-reports.md): a native app's crash. The iPhone and Mac apps write a dump from MetricKit's crash diagnostic (CrashReports.swift: `appdump 1` and its lines, in the schema) and post it to POST /api/playtest/app-crash; room-crash.coax makes the report from it (crash_app_report), and the API keeps it by bucket. A frame is `f BINARY +0xOFFSET`; the build line is the app binary's UUID, which names its dSYM.

Capacity record v1 (#13296, docs/deployment/soak.md): one night's soak of the full fleet. soak.coax writes it through soak-record.coax and posts it to POST /api/playtest/capacity-record (signed as a room's `capacity` write); the API checks it and reads its day, environment, seats and verdict through the same codec (ticket-sign-unit.c), stores the body whole, one a day and environment, and GET /api/playtest/capacity answers the newest as it was kept. The status page reads its lines.

A world's edits v1 (#13412, the browser editor's E3; docs/protocol/world-edit-v1.md): one typed edit (spawn, despawn, set a column, move, rotate, scale, set a content cell, shape the land) and the batch that names the revision it was made from (apply, undo, redo, original, publish-now, publish-next). world-edit.coax writes and reads both and carries an entity edit out on the engine's edit log with its inverse. POST /api/worlds/ID takes a batch (worlds.c reads its head through world-policy.coax); a world's own Coax carries it out (Splice: metaverse/splice/world.coax).

What /api/worlds/ID answers (#13412): a lane's revision, the dev and live revisions, when live's last update reaches sessions, the undo log's steps, and the lane's document (a read) or the batch as it was taken (a write); or a refusal in words naming the edit refused. Pinned in the edit profile beside the batch.

A world's document v1 (#13412; docs/protocol/world-doc-v1.md): the World saved whole (entities, every column, the realm's own columns), the content revision, the edit log's head and the next entity number, with a digest. world-doc.coax writes it (world_save) and loads it (world_load), refusing a document that does not give its own digest. The API stores it as text (verse.world_docs, migration 0181) and carries it unread; Splice's is the game's World (metaverse/splice/world.coax).

Domain event (#13412): an edit to a world was saved. Published by the realm-authoring outbox (verse.world_outbox, lane dev, migration 0181) in the transaction that changes the document, one event a revision; a reader takes the event whose revision is one above the last it took (we_take). Typed fields only: the sequence, the world, the revision, the edit, the time.

Domain event (#13412): a world's dev revision became live. Published by the same outbox on the live lane, with the dev revision it was made from, when it reaches open sessions (now or next) and the pins of the build that reads it (engine, rules, content, wire); metaverse-engine/editor/world-live.coax decides what a session does with it.
Aethyrforge VPK2 asset pack layout (128-entry table, 64 MiB stream bound, 64-slot atomic registry admission; #13244).
A texture layer as GPU blocks with its mip chain (#13305): the layer entries of a pack's block build (NAME.TAG.vpk3), uploaded with writeTexture.

VRG1: skinned rigs as bytes (#13306): up to eight named sets, each two bodies' rests and binds and their clips' key tracks, as anim/skin.coax plays them. The rig entry (kind 7) of an asset pack; Everglade's people, preview and two-hand rigs are written by everglade/model/tools/rig-pack.coax and read by everglade/scene/rig-asset.coax.

ECH1: a character's rig and source-local pose clips, kept byte for byte for Valley playback; read by metaverse-engine/character/rig.coax through this file. Its profile pins one fixture and the damage its reader refuses (#13304).
EFC1: named sparse morphs and source-rate facial curves and local bone samples. Its profile pins one fixture and the damage its reader refuses (#13304).
FRG1: a face rig block, admitted here before the face-rig evaluator sees it. Its profile pins one fixture and the damage its reader refuses (#13304).
RCM1: the resource cost manifest of a streamed world's assets. Its profile pins one fixture and the damage its reader refuses (#13304).
FST1: the fact payload of a realm's state, carried inside AESV and ACK1 envelopes. Its profile pins one fixture and the damage its reader refuses (#13304).
ACK1: the engine's checkpoint envelope. Its profile pins one fixture and the damage its reader refuses (#13304).
HTP1: the whole-container transport companion of a pack (source containers and spans). Its profile pins one fixture and the damage its reader refuses (#13304).

VPK3: a pack's image as pages fetched by HTTP Range, each admitted by SHA-256 (#13001); read by hosts through metaverse-engine/host/page-stream.coax. Its profile pins one fixture and the damage its reader refuses (#13304).

OCM1: the Ocarina import's material records (link.materials, scene.materials), a file between the steps of one local import. One writer and one reader; the material, atlas, foliage and bundle tools go through it. Its profile pins one fixture and the damage its reader refuses (#13304).
Local Aethyrforge scene command v1 (place, move, remove; #13244).
Local Aethyrforge scene command v2 (retains v1 and adds versioned one-object resize; #13244).

The NPC ask, POST /api/playtest/npc/ask, and its answer (#13261). wire.coax writes and reads both; Everglade (everglade/legacy/v1/people.coax), Fairy Forest (metaverse/fairy-forest/talk.coax), the Haunted House (apps/openagents-web/realm.coax) and made realms (apps/openagents-web/myrealm.coax) call it. A hand codec: history is written even when empty and a control byte is written as a space. test_npc.py posts every fixture to the API and gets its status.
The NPC ask's fixtures (npc-ask above): the pages' asks, the bodies the API refuses and its answers, byte for byte.
Local Aethyrforge NPC command v1 (spawn, order, remove with bounded target classes; #13244).
Local Aethyrforge raid command v1 (start, stop, double, wave, set; #13244).

A realm's save (docs/protocol/realm-save-aesv-v1.md): the AESV container with its CRC-32, kept in IndexedDB and in verse.progress; the browser's record of two saves (verse-save 1); and the body that posts a save. save.coax packs and opens it for every realm page. The API checks a posted container in C (player.c container_ok: magic, version, layer, CRC-32); test_player.py posts every golden and malformed container to /api/playtest/progress and gets what the profile's "server" says.

Everglade's city edits, eg-edit 1 (docs/protocol/everglade-edits-v1.md): what an admin adds to the designed city, as text in doc.edits of the realm's published world. edits.coax writes and reads the list, the publish body and the API's answer for the pages (everglade-edit.coax, everglade-voice.coax), Aethyrforge (scene-cli.coax) and the guide (guide-route.coax). The room only notes that a list came (room-world.c) and the API stores the document unread.

A made realm's document, doc aethyr.realm version 1 (#13249; profile verse-doc). The server builds it in SQL and hashes jsonb's text of it per revision; doc.coax reads it (forge_read_doc), writes the same bytes (forge_doc_json) and reads and writes the replies of /save, /undo and /redo (SaveReply, UndoReply, Conflict). One fixture, replayed through edit.coax and doc.coax by doc-goldens.coax and through the routes by realm_doc_checks.coax (coax/web/api/test.sh). A hand codec, not the JSON mapper: the document has objects keyed by name and decimals; the small replies are on the mapper and the check reads them through it too.

A made realm's edits (#13249): the bodies of /save (SaveRequest, forge_save_body) and /undo and /redo (RevRequest, forge_rev_body), and the server's undo log (UndoStep, built in SQL), which doc.coax's forge_apply_step applies to the edit model. The fixture holds each step the server logged; the check applies every one to the model and takes the undo and redo the server took.

A made realm's record (#13250, E11 part 1; profile verse-doc): the bodies of GET /api/playtest/realms/mine (MineReply, and its ?as=lines text), POST .../visibility (VisibilityRequest, VisibilityReply), a made realm's POST .../publish (PublishRequest, PublishReply), GET .../published (PublishRecord) and a realm route's refusal (RouteError). The server builds them in SQL as jsonb's text; record.coax writes and reads the same bytes, and the CLI (realm list, visibility, publish) and My Realm (publish) call it. One fixture, held through the codec by record-goldens.coax and through the routes by realm_record_checks.coax (coax/web/api/test.sh). A hand codec: jsonb's key order and spacing. coax/web/api/realms.c is not in files yet: its other routes and the bytes it writes itself are still on the allowlist.

What coax/web/api/realms.c writes itself (#13250, E11 part 2; profile verse-doc): every refusal the route decides (the API's ErrorReply, through api-wire.coax), `page` added to an SQL answer (Paged: a visibility's as jsonb spells it, a make's and a fork's with no spaces), the card's answer (CardReply), a made realm's lines and a refusal's words for a caller that reads lines. realms.c calls the codec through realm-wire.generated.c and builds no body. The fixture holds the bytes the C wrote before. coax/web/api/realms.c is not in files yet: the bodies its SQL builds for the builder, the text lists and the edit routes have no row. realms.c is this row's route file since every reader is on a codec (#13250): coder realm play reads the spec's character lines through metaverse-engine/editor/spec.coax (coax/lib/media/realm_seat.coax, context realm-seat).

A realm made or forked (#13250, E11 part 3; profile verse-doc): the answer of POST /api/playtest/realms and POST .../<slug>/fork as JSON (MadeReply: SQL's object and the page realms.c adds) and as ?as=lines text (written by coax/web/api/realm-wire.coax), and a fork's body (ForkRequest). made.coax reads both answers and writes the body; the builder (MAKE IT), My Realm (FORK) and the CLI (realm new, realm fork) call it. The fixture is a made realm's forks, held through the codec by made-goldens.coax, which also reads realm-wire.coax's lines goldens, and through the routes by realm_record_checks.coax. Since part 4 it also holds a built-in realm's fork pane: fork info's lines (GET .../<slug>/fork), a fork's publish (ForkPublishRequest, ForkPublishReply) and a built-in fork with its rules; Everglade's pane (apps/openagents-web/everglade-fork.coax) builds and reads all of them through made.coax.

A realm's spec (#13250, E11 part 5): GET /api/playtest/realms/<slug>, text a line each, written in SQL (verse.realm_edit_spec). The profile names all 28 lines. spec.coax is the one reader: it gives each line's kind and its fields, and My Realm (read_spec), the realm edit layer (redit_read, redit_read_rows) and the CLI (forge_spec_value, cli_edit_read_moves) take them from it; each kept its own line splitter before. The fixture holds seven specs as the server answers them (a made realm to its owner, after a save, to a visitor and to nobody, a fork, a hand-built realm); spec-goldens.coax reads every line through the reader and requires it back byte for byte from its fields, and realm_record_checks.coax asks the API for them. Two stand-ins write a spec for checks and are not products: coax/web/cli-journey-fixture.coax and coax/web/room/room-dev.coax.

The realm builder (#13250, E11 part 6): the bodies of POST /api/playtest/realms/plan, /pick and /realms (MAKE IT) (builder.proto's PlanRequest, PickRequest, MakeRequest; profile verse-doc) and the board and the pick as ?as=lines answers them (SQL's verse.builder_lines; the profile names all 11 lines). board.coax writes every body and reads every line: the builder page (ask_plan, ask_pick, make_it, read_board, the pick's value, the setup a dropped document starts from) and the CLI (realm new's two bodies, cli_plan_board) call it; each built and split its own before. The fixture holds the requests as both send them and the answers as the server gives them; board-goldens.coax holds them through the codec and the descriptor, and test_realm_builder.py sends them to the API. The JSON answers (PlanReply, PickReply) have no reader in a product: every product asks for lines; the schema names them and the check holds their keys. plan/doc's body is finished by the page's host (browser glue: it adds the picked file's name and data to the setup board.coax wrote).

A realm's edits (#13250, E11 part 7; profile verse-doc): the bodies of POST .../<slug>/settings, /switch, /revise, /asks, /asks/<id>/done, /place, /lore and /quest (and the same under .../edit-v1/ with the revision first), and what the server answers. change.coax writes every body: the realm edit layer (metaverse/edit/edit.coax), My Realm (a placed thing) and the CLI's edit verbs call it; each built its own before. The fixture holds the bodies as the pages and the CLI send them and the answers as the server gives them, held through the codec and the descriptor by change-goldens.coax and through the routes by realm_record_checks.coax. Three requests go to the planner's model (an ask, a revision, an ask marked done): the fixture holds their bodies only, and the lines an ask answers are the text lists' step. No product reads the JSON answers beyond their status, the revision (doc.coax's forge_read_reply) and whether a deletion deleted (forge_change_deleted). POST .../describe has no caller in a product (the builder sends the line with MAKE IT); the schema names it and the fixture holds it.

A realm's other text answers (#13250, E11 part 8), written in SQL: the feature list (GET .../asks), what an ask, a revision and a dropped document answer, the edit panes (lore, quests), the proposals, the listed realms (GET /realms/listed), the made realms' rows for /og (GET /realms/made) and the card's want. lists.coax reads the asks, the panes and the proposals for the realm edit layer (which read them itself before); listed.coax (moved from apps/openagents-web/realms-listed.coax, its rules unchanged) reads the listed answer for the list page, and its listed_field reads a row's fields for the /og page's made rows; a board's rows are spec.coax's. The CLI prints these lists as they come and reads nothing from them. The fixture holds each as the server answers it; the ask's and the revision's answers need the planner's model and are made by test_realm_builder.py. Not on a codec: the card's want ("want" or "no") is read by coax/web/card.js, browser glue that then takes the picture and posts a JPEG. coax/web/card.js compares the card's want with the one word "want" in the browser: host glue, not a second parser; the word is pinned here.

aethyr-engine 1 (#13249): a published made realm's engine manifest, one attribute a line, and its SHA-256. publish.coax writes it and checks a record read back; the server keeps the same rule in SQL. One fixture pair: publish.coax's #test and realm_engine_pin.sql (run by coax/web/api/test.sh through realm_engine_pin.coax) give the same manifest and hash.
Aethyr Physics Lab LABIN001/LABOUT01 binary records (160-byte input header, 104-byte body table, 180-step/30-sample output snapshots; #13244).

A seat in a running realm (#13250, E11; the feature is #12655; profile api-routes): the bodies of POST /api/playtest/seats (OpenRequest, Grant), GET /api/playtest/seats (SeatsReply), .../keep (Kept) and .../close (Closed), and what the API sends the runner that holds a hosted seat's page (RunnerOpen, RunnerAct, RunnerClose), and the first line the runner hands the seat's own process (SeatStart). The server builds the grant, the list and the act in SQL as jsonb's text; realm_seat_wire.coax writes and reads the same bytes. seats.c calls the codec through seat-wire.generated.c (coax/web/api/seat-wire.coax, which adds the API's ErrorReply from api-wire.coax) and builds no body. One fixture, taken from a running API: seat-wire-goldens.coax holds it through the codec, and test_room.py requires the API's bytes to be the fixture's and runs each through the same check (--read). A hand codec: jsonb's key order and spacing. The CLI (openagents realm play, apps/openagents-cli/realm-play.coax) and the realm's YOUR AGENT pane (metaverse/edit/agent.coax) write the open body and read the grant through the codec. The runner (coax/web/agent/seat-runner.c) reads its three bodies, writes the seat's first line, {"closed":true} and its refusals through seat-runner-wire.c (coax/web/agent/seat-runner-wire.coax) and parses nothing itself; oa-seat (coax/web/agent/seat.coax) reads the first line through the codec; test_room.py holds a running runner to the fixture too. The action of .../act (Action) and the observation it answers (Observation, Near) are the codec's as well: seatw_action_json and seatw_read_action, seatw_obs_json and seatw_read_obs. The CLI and the page write an action and read an observation through it, the seat (coax/lib/media/realm_seat.coax) reads the action and writes the observation, and the local stand-in runner (coax/web/local-origin.coax) does the same. The fixture's observations are lines a seat in a running realm printed in headless Chrome.

The API's refusal body as it ships, {"error":"WORDS"} (#13250; profile api-routes). One writer, aw_error; a route file's own codec loads it and exports the writer its C calls. The spec's openagents.api.v1 envelope is planned and has another shape; a route moves to it with a new version. The goldens' refusals go through the codec and the JSON mapper.

Service levels and alerts (#13297): GET /api/playtest/service-health (Health), the service-watch job's result (WatchResult) and the alerts the job hands verse.service_sync (Wanted). service.c calls the codec through service-wire.generated.c and builds no body. A hand codec: worst is null when nothing was counted, daily is an array of arrays, and the alert lists and the sync answer are jsonb's text carried as it came. test_jobs.py reads the route's body, the job's result and a refusal from a running API through the golden check (--read).
Agent accounts and grants. Generated codec from proto/descriptors/account-agents.pb; the API calls it through agent-wire-unit.c.

A security notice as a push to an app (#13233): the body push.c sends Apple's push service and Google's for each notice auth-recover.c delivers to a device that gave a push target. Our members are the alert's words, the notice's id and kind, and the page the app opens (/settings/security, nothing else); a push carries no link, token or address. push.c builds no body: it calls the codec through auth-push.generated.c. Goldens in the profile; auth-push-goldens.coax writes each through the codec and reads it back.
Haunted House save and scene. Generated codec from proto/descriptors/haunt.pb.
One voice Frame per WebSocket binary message. Generated codec from proto/descriptors/voice.pb.

The iOS home's configuration and its HudInvocation replies. Generated codec from proto/descriptors/ios-home.pb. It writes engine/v1's HudInvocation, so hud.proto has a product consumer. The check needs protoc (PROTOC=...).

Indexed repos (#13326, docs/repos/2026-11-11-indexed-repos.md): the bodies of the repo service oa-repo, POST /api/repo/call and /api/repo/fetch (RepoRequest, RepoAnswer), through the JSON mapper. The service (coax/web/repo/serve.coax) reads requests and writes answers; the chat engine (coax/web/agent/chat.coax) writes requests and reads answers.
The protobuf door of POST /v1/systemone. Generated codec from proto/descriptors/systemone.pb. The JSON request body is the shape systemone-request-json.
Scene, agent, control, state and assets: tests and tools only. hud.proto is not here: metaverse/home.coax writes its HudInvocation.
Used only under coax/tests/. Don't build on it before the room servers' reach is decided.
Imported by presence.proto only.
No Coax or C file imports it. The explorer API it describes (docs/protocol/bitcoin-explorer-v1.md) answers JSON written by hand; a step that moves that API onto this schema takes the status out.
No Coax or C file imports it (docs/protocol/bitcoin-lab-v1.md describes it).
No Coax or C file imports it (docs/protocol/bitcoin-mempool-v1.md describes it).
No Coax or C file imports it (docs/protocol/desk-control-v2.md describes it).
No Coax or C file imports it. The Responses gateway (psionic/lib/responses/) writes its JSON by hand; a step that moves it onto this schema takes the status out.

A field option, not a record: nostr/event/v1alpha2/event.proto imports it and coax/lib/proto/importer.coax reads the option. It is in no profile by name and no product file writes bytes of its own from it.

The #import_proto JSON mapper options (coax/proto.md, "JSON mapper"). Read by the importer, so no profile carries it; used only under coax/tests/proto/ until a producer moves onto the mapper (C3-C6, E1-E6).
host/v1 and reach/v1. A library adapter imports them (coax/lib/nostr/adapters/host-proto-import.coax); only tests and an example load it. coder host uses NIP-HOST's JSON, not this.

The session log (docs/protocol/session-log-v1.md). Package openagents.session.log.v1alpha1; the id on disk stays. log.coax writes every line (C1) and is its one reader (sl_next, sl_read; C2). chat.record builds the same log in SQL for GET /api/chat/record; coax/web/api/test_zchat.py reads every line it returns through log.coax (log-profile.coax --read) and requires each to be written back byte for byte.

A coding agent's run store (#13444, coax/lib/agent/workmem/README.md): the log of what a run read, learned, changed and ran, DIR/log.jsonl, one JSON object a line. store.coax writes every line and is its one reader; file.coax keeps the log and the texts it names by hash; the finish rule over it is finish.coax (#authority).
Two kinds: ReplyDelta and ReplyEnd (profile coder-stream). Aethyrforge's chat reads them through stream.coax (cst_read).
Three kinds: Model, Usage and Availability (profile coder-stream). The check holds every key of the goldens to a json_name and reads and writes availability through the JSON mapper.
Qualification file seal (docs/protocol/coder-qualification-v1.md). Encoded and read by coder/tests/evidence.coax; pinned byte for byte in proto/coder/qualification-v1.json.
Qualification checkpoint seal pairs (docs/protocol/coder-qualification-v1.md). Encoded and read by coder/tests/evidence.coax.
Qualification execution receipt (docs/protocol/coder-qualification-v1.md). Single encoder in coder/tests/evidence.coax with budget_ms as an argument.
Qualification receipt (docs/protocol/coder-qualification-v1.md). Encoded and read by coder/tests/evidence.coax; committed receipts under docs/verification/ re-encoded byte for byte.

The AI-call ledger, ~/.openagents/usage/ai-calls.jsonl. ledger.coax writes it (next.coax's turns, tiers.coax) and reads it (next-context.coax usage, golems.coax); a hand codec, as model_usage carries Claude Code's modelUsage object (floats, keyed by model) byte for byte. Golden lines from both of today's writers.

The next-issue decision, ~/.openagents/everglade/next-issue/decisions.jsonl. Written and read through the JSON mapper (#import_proto) in ledger.coax; next.coax keeps its values and writes the line when the host takes it.
The tier rubric: tier.coax sends its five fields to the model as the answer schema (TIER_PROPERTIES); the decision carries them as scores. A check in ledger.coax holds the two to the Rubric message.

The hosted runner's wire (profile agent-managed): the engine's lines (turn, event, call, reply, stop, done), the event batches and end bodies to the API, and next's answer. One writer, runner-wire.coax: turn.coax and chat.coax load it (engine-line.coax); runner.c and chat-runner.c call it through runner-wire.c, compiled beside them. A hand codec, as the turn and done lines and the end bodies carry doubles; EventLine, StopLine and EventBatch also go through the JSON mapper in the check. test_zchat.py posts the goldens' batches and /chat end bodies to the API and reads back the goldens' chat.events rows.

The sealed credential: AES-256-GCM, base64 of nonce, ciphertext and tag, with the associated data oa-chat-credential.v1|OWNER|KIND (rw_aad). The golden seals a fixed TEST key, nonce, owner and kind to fixed bytes, checked with coax/lib/crypto/aes_gcm.coax and with the runner's OpenSSL seal (runner_seal_check.c, from test_zchat.py).

The agents running on this computer, as `openagents coder agents --json` and `coder agents --json` print them (#13250, C7; profile cli-local). coax/lib/local/inventory-wire.coax writes it (processes.coax la_json calls it) and reads it (the Metaverse Engine's setup). The fixture holds reports a build host's CLI printed.
The installed checkpoints, as `openagents models ls --json` and `models verify parakeet --json` print them (#13250, C7). Same codec and fixture as the agents report.

`openagents dictate --events|--json`, one JSON object a line (#13250, C7; profile cli-local). coax/lib/local/dictation-wire.coax writes it for the CLI and reads it for Coder's terminal dictation. The fixture holds lines real runs printed, every type and every status state; apps/openagents-cli/tests/dictate-check.coax and coder/tui/dictation_check.coax run the CLI and Coder end to end.

`openagents dictate --stream --events` (#13250, C7; docs/protocol/dictation-stream-v1.md). Same codec and fixture as the final-only events: every type and every status state, from docs/verification/dictate-stream-2026-11-03.

What coder session-read, the coder_session_read tool and coder mcp answer about another tool's conversations (profile coder-session-reader). claude-history.coax holds every opening of the envelope and writes a page; coder/tui/session-reader.coax adds a list's rows. The fixture is replies the Coder CLI printed, with the transcripts it read: the check holds each reply's keys to its message and requires the writer's exact bytes from the transcript. Its readers are models and MCP clients. docs/protocol/coder-session-reader-v1.md.

Microcoder's durable journal AJR1 (sessions/worker-US.ajr): hash-chained binary frames, hand-packed. aj_prepare writes a frame and aj_read reads one; the worker and replay call nothing else. The profile's frames were made with Python's hashlib, not the codec; journal-profile.coax --file walks a journal a worker wrote. docs/protocol/microcoder-journal-ajr1.md.

What Microcoder sends the model each step: the system prompt (loop.coax MC_SYSTEM), the answer schema (action.coax MC_SCHEMA) and the state (state.coax mc_state_json). The profile is the bytes for one fixed session of six steps; the check requires them byte for byte, requires each state to begin with the one before it (the prompt cache's prefix), and reads the profile's replies through mc_action_parse. docs/protocol/microcoder-prompt-v1.md.

The consent ledger, ~/.openagents/coder/consent/events.jsonl: one event of psionic/lib/harness/consent.coax a line, hash-chained. gt_line writes a line and gt_unline reads one; Coder (coder/tui/gate.coax) and the Metaverse Engine's chat open and save the ledger through this file. The fixture is ledgers the Coder CLI wrote. docs/protocol/consent-memory-ledgers-v1.md.

Coder's memory log, ~/.openagents/coder/memory/events.jsonl: one event of psionic/lib/harness/memory.coax a line, hash-chained, its bytes in hex. mem_line writes a line and mem_unline reads one; coder/tui/memory.coax loads and saves the log through this file. The fixture is a log the Coder CLI wrote. docs/protocol/consent-memory-ledgers-v1.md.

Golemancy's cache of GitHub answers. Kept local.
ID.pid, ID.stop, ID.turnstop, ID.answer, ID.inbox/*.msg, ID.acp, ID.remote beside a session log. Same machine. Also used by coder/tui/router.coax, host.coax, acp.coax and remote.coax.

NIP-HOST's grant. Anticorruption layer: coax/lib/nostr/host/grant.coax is the only file that parses this format, and its output is our own record type (HsGrant).

Nostr events and the NIPs; proto/nostr/ holds the pinned projections. Anticorruption layer: coax/lib/nostr/ is the only folder that parses raw Nostr wire events, and its output is our own record type (NsEvent and typed NIP projections).
LNURL and Lightning Addresses. Anticorruption layer: coax/lib/lnaddr/ is the only folder that parses LNURL-pay replies, and its output is our own record types (LnPayInfo, LnInvoice).
